name: Murloc
summary: Murlocs are amphibious, bipedal humanoids famous for their gurgling battle cries, territorial coastal villages, and sudden swarming tactics. Though historically dwelling in the deep ocean, they have steadily migrated inland along the shores, lakes, and rivers of Azeroth, acting with far greater coordination and cunning than their primitive appearance suggests.

sections.title: Creatures of the Shallows
sections.body: Murlocs dwell in densely populated settlements along coastlines, riverbanks, and freshwater lakes. Averaging roughly four feet in height, they possess bulbous, slime-coated bodies, wide mouths filled with sharp fangs, and keen vision capable of piercing pitch-black water. While individuals are rarely seen wandering far from their kin, encountering one murloc invariably means a dozen more lurk just beneath the surface. They rely on overwhelming numbers and sharp crude weaponry.

sections.title: The Inland March
sections.body: Though ancient lineages suggest murlocs have existed beneath the waves since before recorded history, their widespread encroachment onto the landmasses of Lordaeron and Kalimdor is relatively recent. Historians note that this inland migration coincided suspiciously with the reemergence of the serpentine naga from the ocean depths. Some tribes appear to worship deep-sea monstrosities waiting in the oceanic fathoms. Whether fleeing darker terrors or preparing the world for their masters' awakening, their coordinated movement into freshwaters poses a rising threat.

sections.title: A Hidden Intellect
sections.body: Because their garbled language sounds like nonsensical bubbling to outsiders, many dismiss murlocs as mere feral pests. However, their coordinated ambushes, mastery of earth and water magic, and communal structures hint at a sharper intellect. Renowned explorer Brann Bronzebeard has suggested that murlocs are far smarter than civilized races realize, intentionally concealing their cunning. Their impact on global history is undeniable: it was a murloc raid upon the Darkspear tribe that spurred Thrall to intervene, forging the alliance between the orcs and trolls that built the modern Horde.

faq.q: Why do murlocs attack all at once?
faq.answer: Murlocs rarely fight alone. They live in tight-knit, crowded settlements and respond in groups to intruders, swarming enemies with overwhelming numbers.

Yes, far more than their comical appearance implies. While their guttural, gurgling dialect is incomprehensible to most, murlocs craft weapons, organize strategic ambushes, and wield elemental water and earth magic. Scholars like Brann Bronzebeard believe murlocs intentionally allow outsiders to underestimate their intellect.

faq.q: Why are murlocs moving inland from the sea?
faq.answer: Originally creatures of the ocean floor, murlocs have steadily advanced into freshwater lakes and riverbeds. Historians suspect this migration was triggered by the resurgence of the naga or by deep-sea entities slumbering in the abyss whose awakening commands murlocs to secure the land.

faq.q: How did murlocs help form the Horde?
faq.answer: During the Third War, a tribe of murlocs serving the sea witch Zar'jira ambushed the Darkspear trolls on their island home. Warchief Thrall and his orc warriors fought alongside Sen'jin to defend the trolls. This battle forged the unbreakable bond between orcs and the Darkspear tribe, laying the foundation of the modern Horde.
Mur'gul are murlocs encountered during the Third War. Despite their strange appearance and name, they are living creatures.

faq.q: What is that iconic sound murlocs make?
faq.answer: When engaging prey or raising the alarm, murlocs let out a loud, wet, undulating gargle (often rendered as 'Aaaaaughibbrgubugbugrguburgle' or 'RwlRwlRwlRwl'). It serves as both an aggressive psychological weapon and an instant call for their pack to converge.

angles.text: The Darkspear tribe shares a bitter history with murlocs, having faced capture and ritual sacrifice by coastal tribes before joining Warchief Thrall.
Thrall's warriors fought murlocs while rescuing the Darkspear trolls at sea, learning early on that their goofy demeanor hides savage brutality.
Settlers across Westfall, Darkshore, and Lakeshire frequently find their shipping, farms, and docks besieged by encroaching murloc tribes.
Murloc mystics possess an innate, if crude, connection to water and earth elementals, bending the local spirits to bolster their shoreline villages.
